title: Implement debounce
description:
Implement `debounce(func, wait)`.

It returns a new function that postpones calling `func` until `wait` milliseconds have passed since the **last** time the new function was called. Every call restarts the wait. When `func` finally runs, it receives the arguments and the `this` value of the most recent call.

Calls made after `func` has run start a fresh wait. The debounced function itself returns `undefined`.

**Example:** with `wait = 100`, calls at 0 ms and 50 ms run `func` once, at 150 ms, with the arguments of the call made at 50 ms.

**Constraints:** `0 <= wait <= 10000`. Each debounced function keeps its own timer.

### How the tests work

Each test is a short script that calls your function and returns what it observed. Time is virtual: `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearTimeout`, `Date.now()` and `performance.now()` all read a test clock, and time only passes when a test calls `await clock.tick(ms)`. A test may use `spy()`, which returns a function that records every call as `{ args, at }` in `spy.calls`.

exampleTestCases.explanation: The call at 50 ms restarts the wait, so func runs once, at 150 ms, with the latest argument.
Two calls separated by a quiet period run func twice.
